dct_description_sm: Muskoxen are an important native species for the ecosystem, people's subsistence and communities' economic opportunities. They are known to be sensitive to diseases and may constitute a good early indicator of disease trends in the Kitikmeot. The transmission patterns and impacts of many pathogens (viruses, bacteria and parasites) are highly sensitive to environmental conditions, and this becomes a particular concern in the Arctic where significant and rapid climate change is already altering ecosystem dynamics. A better understanding of the influence of pathogens and periodic monitoring of their occurrence will provide key information for the management of the muskox populations and the design of a plan to sustain subsistence harvesting and commercial ventures using muskox populations. 1) Develop a standard monitoring protocol for muskoxen in the Kitikmeot and develop and assess the efficacy of surveillance strategies for ongoing disease surveillance in areas of food safety, muskox health and conservation of muskoxen (an EcoHealth approach), 2) Document the prevalence of diseases in various muskox populations, 3) Enhance hunter education and knowledge about disease and disease sampling techniques, 4) Monitor spatial and temporal trends in muskox diseases prevalence, 5) Use vegetation maps and muskox distribution data to model the probability of disease occurrence and spread, 6) Understand the role of disease in muskox population dynamics, 7) Assess the use of muskox as an indicator species for ungulate diseases in Nunavut, and 8) Use this information to manage muskox populations and other species when necessary.
